paper.title_en: Axion-Like Particle Searches at Muon Colliders: Photon-Neutrino Signatures and Heavy-Neutral-Lepton Feasibility
paper.abstract_en: We study the mono-photon signature $μ^+μ^-\toγa\toγν\barν$ at $3$ and $10\TeV$ muon colliders, with integrated luminosities of $1$ and $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, in a two-coupling axion-like-particle (ALP) simplified model. Five benchmarks spanning $m_a=100$--$1000\GeV$ are generated at $g_{aγγ}=0.01\TeV^{-1}$ and flavor-universal pseudoscalar neutrino couplings $y_ν=0.1$ or $0.3$, giving invisible branching fractions above 99.995% and mono-photon cross sections of $0.00854$--$0.01217\,\mathrm{fb}$. Assuming a 1% background normalization uncertainty, a cut-based photon-line selection gives projected 95% sensitivity to $g_{aγγ}\simeq0.039$--$0.045\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0137$--$0.0140\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. A ROOT/TMVA gradient-boosted decision tree with validation-fixed thresholds reaches held-out AUC values of $0.9967$--$0.9993$ and $g_{95}=0.0192$--$0.0400\TeV^{-1}$ at $3\TeV$ and $0.0122$--$0.0144\TeV^{-1}$ at $10\TeV$. Because only 2-41 irreducible-background test events populate the optimized classifier tails, the mass--coupling contours are reported as projected expected sensitivities rather than profile-likelihood or CL$_s$ exclusions. A separate appendix records a phenomenological, parton-level HNL diphoton feasibility study; it is not used to claim detector-level sensitivity or exclusion.\keywords{Axion-like particles, muon collider, mono-photon, diphoton, heavy neutral leptons, neutrinos, multivariate analysis, effective field theory
